approved: Unlocking Supply of Family Homes Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would let people put more of their home sale proceeds into superannuation and start doing so at a younger age.
It changes the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997 to lower the eligible age, lengthen the contribution window, and raise the maximum amount that can be contributed.
The minimum age would drop from 55 to 50, the period to make a contribution after settlement would grow from 90 days to 1 year, and the cap would rise from $300,000 to $500,000.
Lowers the minimum age for making a downsizer contribution from 55 to 50.
Extends the time allowed after settlement to make the contribution from 90 days to 1 year.
Raises the maximum downsizer contribution from $300,000 to $500,000.
Older Australians who sell their family home and want to contribute the proceeds to superannuation.

Moved the second reading of the Unlocking Supply of Family Homes Bill 2025, proposing to lower downsizer eligibility from 55 years to 50 years, extend the contribution period from 90 days to 1 year and increase the maximum contribution from $300,000 to $500,000; debate was adjourned.

Supported the Unlocking Supply of Family Homes Bill 2025, proposing to lower the downsizer contribution age from 55 to 50, extend the contribution period from 90 days to one year and increase the limit from $300,000 to $500,000 per person. Argued that the changes could improve housing supply and retirement flexibility.
